Working with AI Agents

Ivan Jacob Agaloos Pesigan

Source: vignettes/agents.Rmd
agents.Rmd

This vignette describes how coding agents work on an rProject project: who does what, which keywords start which work, and how a machine is set up for them.

Who does what

Who Does
The user decides; edits in Overleaf; pushes from Overleaf; runs make all and make auto
The main session specs, decisions, code, prose, upload folders, and logs
Claude agents (Sonnet, Haiku) work that waits, reads long logs, or repeats across projects
Codex, Copilot, Antigravity run the same keywords inline when they are the agent in use

Agents never push to Overleaf, and push to GitHub only when the user’s message or keyword asks for it.

Keywords

Keyword Does Engine in Claude Code
O2G verify and record the user’s Overleaf push verify (Haiku)
PUB check the public repository and its CI pub-check (Sonnet)
build docs, build docs only, build sif publish the docker images and rebuild docs.sif and docs-plus.sif build-docs (Sonnet)
build rProject build and publish rProject from a verified private push the main session
build lib publish the lib-* libraries and rebuild the bibliographies the main session
CI <project> wait for the last push’s runs and read the failed logs ci-watch (Sonnet)
rollout <set> <target> run a make target across projects, stopping at the first failure rollout (Sonnet)
sim status <project> count a simulation’s jobs against its design sim-status (Haiku)
EX, handoff update claude.txt and .setup/ai/handoff.md the main session
start a fresh session: read the handoff and todo.txt, check what is pending, wait the main session

An upload folder also starts the o2g-watch agent (Haiku). A keyword is the request to spawn its agent. Other work is spawned only when the user asks.

make aiglobal, in rProject, installs the global instructions and the agent files of inst/ai/agents/ into ~/.claude/agents/. An agent that leaves rProject is removed there; one the user added stays.

When to delegate

A subagent starts cold, so it pays only for work that waits (over about five minutes), reads a lot (logs and diffs over about 200 lines), or repeats (three or more projects). A short check stays in the main session, as do edits, prose, decisions, and upload folders.

Rules for delegated work

  • Read-only, except the records make verify RECORD=TRUE writes.
  • Evidence, not inference: quote a failure from the log and a deletion from git diff --name-status.
  • Never edit a running script. Wait in the shell, not in a model.
  • A report of under 300 words; a stopped run is never restarted without the user.

Long jobs

Start a long job detached, write the handoff, and end the session; a new session reads the status file. build-docs.sh and build-rproject.sh run from a copy of themselves, so an edit to the file cannot reach a running build. The images build as a Slurm job (account open, 1 core, 16 GB, 12 h), and make all in “build rProject” runs on a compute node; BUILD=host overrides either.

Session habits

  • One release per session: after a verified O2G or PUB, write the handoff and start fresh.
  • Upload folders are final once given. A later change goes in a new folder.
  • A cheaper model for a whole session of routine steps: /model sonnet.

Running in the image

R runs only inside Apptainer. Write the binds in every command:

apptainer exec -B ~/work:$(readlink -f ~/work) <image> make <target>

~/work is a symlink on some machines and a folder on others. A bare -B ~/work fails where it is a symlink, because the container sees the link but not its target. On Roar, add -B /scratch/ibp5092. APPTAINER_BIND, set in ~/.bash-variables, covers commands typed in an interactive shell; with both, Apptainer warns that the destination is already in the mount list, and the command still runs. apptainer build fails with the variable set, because %post applies the bind: use env -u APPTAINER_BIND apptainer build ..., as build-docs.sh does.

Setting up a machine 

bash inst/shell/setup-machine.sh [--force] [--check] [--image <sif>]

On the host, this installs the machine tools and the command line tools, moves the large ones to ~/work/tools (linked from home) where ~/work exists, installs the dotfiles, and runs make local in the image. --check also runs make all: not on a submit node. Then sign in to each command line tool once.

bash inst/shell/install.sh machine   # apptainer claude codex copilot antigravity herdr gh
bash inst/shell/install.sh cli       # fzf zoxide bat fd eza delta
bash inst/shell/install.sh --list    # versions, and where each tool lives
bash inst/shell/install.sh --move    # move what is installed to ~/work/tools

The dotfiles are in inst/dotfiles. make dotfiles or bash inst/shell/install-dotfiles.sh installs them, keeping each file it replaces in ~/.dotfiles-backup; --check shows the differences and changes nothing. make all does not install them. ~/.bash-local is for what belongs to one machine.

Changing a decision

Each decision here is a line in .setup/ai/global/AGENTS.md, an agent file in inst/ai/agents/, or a script option. Change the source, then run make aiglobal on each machine.
